items.response: I'll open the PR for the editor store refactor. The zustand store matches ADR 0009, so I'll mention that in the description. Action: check the current branch and diff against main, run the checks quickly, push the branch and open the PR with a summary, and leave the merge to you.

The worker exposes Prometheus metrics on port 9464 at /metrics, so they end up in whatever Prometheus scrapes that endpoint and then show up in Grafana. I haven't verified the scrape setup or the exact metric name for billing-sync queue depth. Action: check the worker helm chart for a ServiceMonitor or scrape config and grep the worker code for the queue depth metric, then build the panel on the real metric name.

I'll add pino redaction on the API logger for authorization headers, cookies and token fields, plus scrub Bearer tokens out of error messages, since path-based redact won't catch a token embedded in a message string. Everything stays ESM with import syntax, no require(), and pino only, no console.log. Action: look at the api logger setup, add the redact config and a message scrubber, and add a test that logs a bearer token in a header and an error and asserts it is masked.

Doing items 1 and 3 from Lena's blocking list, and leaving the tests to you. The error state will win over empty in the table, and the empty state markup moves out of table.tsx into the new component. Action: create components/invoices/empty-state.tsx from the table.tsx markup, render the error state before the empty state at table.tsx:140, and keep the rest of the diff small.

Got it: #1189 is approved and checks are green, so it's ready for you to merge. I won't merge it myself; I'll make sure everything is pushed and leave the merge to you. Summary to follow as a short list: approved and green, nothing merged by me. Action: confirm the branch is fully pushed, then post a short bullet-list summary of what's in the PR.

Uploads go directly to S3 with presigned URLs from POST /v1/uploads, so the receipt PDF shouldn't pass through our API body. The flow is: form file field, request a presigned URL, upload straight to S3, then save the returned reference on the expense so the file ends up in S3. Action: read the POST /v1/uploads handler and the expense form and schema to see what it accepts and returns, then wire the field with PDF type and size checks and tests.

The API pool max is 10 connections per pod, and the agreement with Priya was to scale pods, not the pool. So I wouldn't raise it. Pool size times max pods has to stay under the PgBouncer limit, so the staging error likely means that product is too high. Action: check staging's pod count and the PgBouncer limit, and compare against 10 per pod.

There's already a slugify in apps/api/src/lib/slug.ts, but the CLI package shouldn't import from the api app, so I'll write the helper in packages/cli/src/util/slug.ts as you asked and match its behavior. 'Northwind Studio, Inc.' becomes 'northwind-studio-inc'. A shared util is a possible follow-up. Action: read the api slug.ts, write the CLI helper and a few Vitest tests (your example, accents, extra punctuation, empty string), and run them.

A sticky header needs position: sticky with top: 0 and an opaque background on the header cells, and it only works if no ancestor between the table and the scrolling container has overflow hidden. Action: find the invoices table component and its scroll container, make the header sticky, and check it visually and with the web tests.

The repo pins a Node version in .nvmrc (20.11 as far as I know), so I'll nvm install and nvm use before installing, and use pnpm only, version 9 via the packageManager pin, never npm or yarn. I'll verify the pins in the repo rather than trust memory. Action: cd ~/code/acme-platform, read .nvmrc and package.json, run nvm install and nvm use, then pnpm install; seed-demo needs Postgres running and DATABASE_URL set, so I'll only do that if you want demo data.

I'll add an atomic idempotency check before sending, keyed on something stable for the reminder (such as the invoice and reminder type, or the message id if it survives redelivery), claimed with SET NX or a unique constraint so a redelivered message is skipped. I'll check whether the message id stays the same on redelivery. Action: read invoice-reminder.ts and how other worker jobs store state, implement the check, and add a test that delivers the same message twice and asserts a single send.

I'll draft the Slack message from the repo's actual setup docs instead of from memory. For the csv export fix, I'll get it release-ready, but I won't tag, publish or deploy anything without your go. Action: read the README or onboarding doc for the setup steps and draft the message, then find the csv fix branch, confirm tests pass, and prepare the PR and a customer-facing release note, asking you before any release.

Bull Board is mounted at /admin/queues on the worker, behind basic auth, so that's your UI for the email queue jobs. It only works while the worker is running. I don't know the worker's local port or the auth credentials, so I'll look them up rather than guess. Action: check the worker's port and the basic auth env vars, start the worker, and give you the URL to open.

I don't know why there are two; it could be a migration half-done or one used by a specific part of the app. Action: read apps/web/package.json, grep the imports for each auth package, and check git log for when each was added, then tell you which is live and whether the other can go.

On Fastify 5 I'll add a small plugin using an onResponse hook that logs through request.log, so the x-request-id requestId is attached automatically, with method, the matched route pattern rather than the raw URL, status code and duration in ms from reply.elapsedTime. Action: find where plugins live in apps/api, add and register the timing plugin, and add an app.inject test checking the log fields.
